proposal.thesis: Natera is the universe's top scan setup (7.9) and is pulling back inside an uptrend after a reversal from a record $437.41 high on 10/6. WebSearch (Investing.com, Quiver, Weiss, 10/6) attributes that drop to profit-taking, a biotech-wide down day (XBI about -3.4%) and disclosed 10b5-1 executive sales, with no negative company news; the bundle confirms every insider sale in 120 days was a 10b5-1 plan trade. Fundamentals carry the move: revenue $752.75M for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (+50.0% y/y per bundle statements) with positive TTM FCF of $84.2M, institutions read as accumulating with price rising, and sell-side targets were raised this week (Citi $480 on 10/6, Barclays $475 on 10/7). It holds $398 flat today in a defensive tape. Sized as an honest half-risk calibration probe because the 10/6 bar is a reversal off a high, 30-day EPS revisions are -3.6%, and the stock trades near 21x sales. Stop under the 20-day average per KB-7057672046; exit before the 11/5 print.

Today's tape is defensive, and NTRA is a healthcare diversifier (corr 0.15 to the book, beta 1.01) whose thesis is clinical test volume, not AI spend, so it lowers the book's 1.65 beta instead of adding to the AI stack.
proposal.risk_map: Kill if price closes below $372 (under the ~$377 20-day average, the 10/6 reversal extending into a real breakdown), if consensus EPS is cut more than another 5%, or if biotech/diagnostics peers keep selling off together (XBI, GH) while SPY holds, which would make 10/6 the start of sector distribution rather than a one-day flush. Early tell: failure to reclaim the $412 anchored VWAP within two weeks.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: the bundle's mean target is $377.43, about 5% below price, with a strong_buy mean of 1.39 across 22 analysts and 30-day EPS revisions down 3.6%, and the 10/6 reversal reads as a top after a 91% six-month run. MY VIEW: the 10/6 drop was a sector flush plus 10b5-1 disclosure noise, not a change in the business, and the pullback inside an uptrend with institutions accumulating resumes toward a new high before the print. MECHANISM: the mean target is stale, built before this week's raises to $475-$480, and the revenue line (+50% y/y in the June quarter) is outrunning the multiple worries; the EPS revisions reflect losses on a company valued on test volume, not earnings. RESOLUTION: a daily close back above $412 (anchored VWAP) and then $420 by 2026-10-23, and the run-up into the 2026-11-05 Q3 report.
